title: Version-pinned citation anchor and redirect-chain integrity tribunal
hypothesis: A deterministic citation-anchor contract can distinguish an authorized canonical alias from a redirect, fragment, version, host, or source-role substitution and can reject silent identity drift before a citation is counted as support.
null_or_failure: A redirect changes authority root, a fragment moves to a different claim, a floating latest URL substitutes for a frozen version, two aliases are double counted as independent sources, an insecure scheme is accepted, or link resolution is treated as evidence that the cited claim is true.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Mutate version pins, fragments, authority roots, redirect depth, schemes, canonical aliases, source roles, and independence labels; require identity drift and alias double counting to fail closed without performing private or credentialed network access.
rollback_or_recovery: Quarantine the drifting citation, retain the failed vector, restore the last frozen canonical identifier and source role, and require a separately reviewed source update before support can be counted again.
boundary: Citation identity control is local provenance evidence, not proof that a source claim is true or independent.
